rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Snoopy's Cat Fight
rows.synopsis: Charlie Brown can't pitch, Sally's struggles in school, Charlie Brown and Peppermint Patty share a desk, Lucy finds new ways to annoy Schroder. Lastly Snoopy, Linus, and Woodstock fight the cat next door for Linus' blanket.
rows.situation: Giving away the one thing that comforts you, needing it back, and facing a huge scary cat to get it.
rows.notes: Script tier: Gestdown subtitle transcript (Addic7ed), identity check passed (episode title matches; content confirms spring training opener, show-and-tell, shared desk, blanket to Eudora, cat fight). Single row on dominant story per spec: the cat fight that titles the episode and closes it, Linus needing Snoopy to win his blanket back from the enormous cat next door. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: Charlie Brown shakes through his big pitching chance and Linus gets the hug instead (disappointment); Peppermint Patty berates Charlie Brown across a shared desk. No controlled topic fits the cat story; left empty by design. Content: comic dog-cat-boy-and-bird brawl.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Snoopy: Team Manager
rows.synopsis: Lucy's garden, Re-Run's life, Linus looses his blanket, and Snoopy manages the baseball team.
rows.situation: Getting blamed for a loss, quitting over it, and finding out how hard the other side's job is.
rows.notes: Script tier: Gestdown subtitle transcript (Addic7ed), identity check passed (episode title matches; content confirms garden, Rerun on the bike, mailed blanket, Snoopy managing). Single row on dominant story per spec: Snoopy hired as team manager, quits when Charlie Brown scolds him, and the team loses under him; Lucy and Charlie Brown learn running the club is hard and blame is easy to hand out. Coping anchors to Lucy's own walk-back and rehiring of Snoopy. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: Rerun dreads the daily bike ride with the big hole and the German shepherd (he says fear took five pounds off him); Linus mails his blanket to himself and panics that it is lost until the April Fool reveal that Snoopy has it. Topics anchored to the baseball story.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Linus and Lucy
rows.synopsis: Sally gets Snoopy's help with a school assignment, the gang plays football and plays in the snow, Lucy fawns over Schroder, Charlie has a kite flying fiasco, and the various ways Lucy tortures Linus.
rows.situation: Feeling fed up and low until a bickering sibling names one thing to be thankful for.
rows.notes: Script tier: Gestdown subtitle transcript (Addic7ed), identity check passed (episode title matches; content confirms Snoopy-assisted school report, football in snow, kite fiasco, sibling beats). Single row on dominant story per spec: the Linus and Lucy sibling thread, ending with the counting-blessings beat where the low-feeling kid hears 'you have a little brother who loves you'. Coping anchors to reframing/distraction (count your blessings), explicitly shown. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: the kite fiasco (string tangled in Peppermint Patty's nose, kite drags Charlie Brown to school for show and tell); Lucy's failed snowball; the baseball kiss forfeited at home plate. No controlled topic fits the sibling story; left empty by design. Content: comic snow and kite slapstick.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Lucy vs. the World
rows.synopsis: Lucy has to put up with a lot; but she can also dish it out with the best of them whether it's playing baseball, or putting up with her brother. Other stories include Peppermint Patty staying at Charlie Brown's house and Snoopy is nominated for an award.
rows.situation: Handing out criticism all season, then finding out how much it stings when the criticism is yours to take.
rows.notes: Script tier: Gestdown subtitle transcript (Addic7ed), identity check passed (episode title matches; content confirms baseball arc, house guest, Puppy Cup, crabby scroll, baby brother). Single row on dominant story per spec: Lucy's season on the team and in right field, getting cut, and striking back through the school paper; the loss lands on the team anyway. Who learns what: Lucy learns criticism can be dished back, and Charlie Brown practices saying the hard cut ('this is very hard for me to say') to her face, which anchors coping. Lucy's retaliation is shown and does not work, noted honestly. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: Peppermint Patty's letdown guest stay at the Brown house (disappointment); Snoopy loses the Daisy Hill Puppy Cup and refuses dinner (disappointed, comfort offered); Linus thrown out by Lucy, new baby brother arrives. Content: name-calling and yelling between kids.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Linus' Security Blanket
rows.synopsis: Linus gives his blanket away; Peppermint Patty and Charlie Brown get into a fight at school; Schroeder fears that his piano-playing days are over.
rows.situation: Trying to give up the comfort thing you still need, making it through without it, and getting pulled back in.
rows.notes: Script tier: Gestdown subtitle transcript (Addic7ed), identity check passed (episode title matches; content confirms blanket handover, sport coats, apology to neighbors, Poe report, dog-hug). Single row on dominant story per spec: Linus hands his blanket to Snoopy to break the habit, endures two sleepless days, makes it through the weekend, then relapses when Lucy's well-meant replacement gift arrives; his closing line: damage is done by people who thought they were doing the right thing. Coping anchors to asking for help (he recruits Snoopy and sets the rules); the comic betrayal and the relapse are shown and named in the row, not smoothed over. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: Snoopy's rescue of the 'cat' that proves to be a glove and the apology to the neighbors; the called game that floats Charlie Brown off the mound; Schroeder's Beethoven birthday; Lucy's 1,000-day crabby scroll. No controlled topic fits the blanket story; left empty by design.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Snoopy: Man's Best Friend
rows.synopsis: Snoopy is a complex dog. Various stories include his amorous side, his playful side, his role as a protector, a watchdog, and even a rescue dog.
rows.situation: Being scared to sleep alone at night while a parent works late, until a companion comes to stay.
rows.notes: Script tier: Gestdown subtitle transcript (Addic7ed), identity check passed (episode title matches; content confirms the night-alone thread, burglar arc, beagle scout hike, woods rescue, playground arc). Single row on dominant story per spec: Peppermint Patty falling asleep at school because she is afraid to be home alone while her dad works until two, and Snoopy staying over as her watcher; she says she feels safe because he is guarding her. Coping anchors to asking for comfort (a companion's presence at bedtime), with asking for help shown in how it is arranged. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: Charlie Brown lost in a snowy woods, found by Peppermint Patty and Marcie by following comic-book pages (scared, rescued by friends); the burglar arc where the watchdog fails; the playground arc where 'speak softly and carry a beagle' fails against bullies, shown failing and left untagged as a lesson. Age-band edge call: bully confrontation content sits at the top of 5-7; kept 5-7 because the dominant thread is the bedtime fear. No controlled topic fits; left empty by design.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Snoopy the Psychiatrist
rows.synopsis: Lucy picks on Charlie Brown driving him to seek help from Snoopy. Charlie Brown and Linus try to fly a kite. Peppermint Patty and Snoopy go to a dance. Thiebault borrows Charlie Brown's baseball mitt and then insults Peppermint Patty and Marcie.
rows.situation: Being talked down to until the bad feeling about yourself sends you looking for someone to help.
rows.notes: Script tier: Gestdown subtitle transcript (Addic7ed), identity check passed (episode title matches; content confirms psychiatry booth, kite-eating tree, turnabout dance, Thiebault glove arc). Single row on dominant story per spec: Lucy's pebble-and-boulder rundown of Charlie Brown, his declared insecurity, and the psychiatric booth visit where the beagle doctor is asleep. Coping anchors to asking for help; the help comically fails and no tidy resolution is shown, recorded honestly rather than smoothed. Age-band edge call, Batch 9 pattern: kept 5-7 for the insecurity theme but the sustained verbal put-downs (pebble versus boulder, wishy-washy, rope turning for thousands) are sarcasm layers that land better at 8-10, so tagged 8-10 with this reason. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: the kite that explodes and meets the kite-eating tree; Peppermint Patty punching the kid who insulted her date and being made to leave the dance; Thiebault keeping the glove until Marcie belts him. Topics: dominant story fits none of the eight; left empty by design. Content: persistent teasing and name-calling.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: You Can't Win, Charlie Brown
rows.synopsis: Charlie Brown and Snoopy discuss puppy training, Rerun contributes to the baseball team, Lucy and Linus play in the snow, and Peppermint Patty and Marcie in school among many others.
rows.situation: Finally winning the game you have lost your whole life, then having the win taken away.
rows.notes: Script tier: Gestdown subtitle transcript (Addic7ed), identity check passed (episode title matches; content confirms Rerun joining, the first-ever win, the league office, the forfeit, the blanket closet, the kite). Single row on dominant story per spec: Rerun's nickel bet voids the team's first-ever win; Charlie Brown is disgraced, Rerun is sorry ('I didn't know it was wrong, I'm new in the world'), and the title irony lands. Coping: left empty with reason, no listed strategy is shown; the forfeit stands and the episode ends on Lucy's backhanded compliment that Rerun was the first with the courage to bet on the team. Age-band edge call: the gambling-forfeit satire needs a kid who can follow the concept, tagged 8-10 on Batch 9's heavier-beat pattern. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: Lucy locking Linus' blanket in the closet for two weeks (nervous/worried, hands shaking, 'nobody cares'); the kite confidence chant that fails. Content: mild gambling theme.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: The Lost Ballpark
rows.synopsis: Charlie Brown walks funny, Marcie finds her mean streak after a boy develops a crush on her, Linus and Snoopy go truffle hunting, and Charlie Brown's team suffers setback after setback.
rows.situation: Losing the place where you play through no fault of your own, and waiting on the grown-up rules that took it.
rows.notes: Script tier: Gestdown subtitle transcript (Addic7ed), identity check passed (episode title matches; content confirms the vacant-lot loss, liability and umpire rules, golf-ball substitute, Spike's coyote purchase, truffle hunt, Floyd's crush). Single row on dominant story per spec: the team's field is closed over insurance and liability, Charlie Brown copes by bouncing a golf ball against the steps while the field is finally bought back by coyotes arranged by Spike. Coping left empty with reason: no listed strategy is shown working; Lucy's 'fight back' scolding lands, and the fix comes from outside Charlie Brown, recorded honestly. Age-band edge call: the liability and insurance satire reads 8-10 on Batch 9's heavier-beat pattern; the feelings (losing your place to play) are simple, but the plot needs the age. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: Marcie's mean streak against the boy who calls her lamb cake, softened by her own reflection that nicknames are not always serious; Linus and Snoopy's truffle hunt and the Truffles letters (jealousy at Snoopy's picnic). Topics anchored to the baseball story.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Snoopy's Football Career
rows.synopsis: Peppermint Patty is accused of stealing her teacher's gold stars and she enlists Snoopy's help. Linus claims someone stole his blanket. Schroder's piano playing elicits many varied reactions. The gang tries to teach each other how to play football.
rows.situation: Learning a new game with a friend and getting every step comically wrong, over and over.
rows.notes: Script tier: Gestdown subtitle transcript (Addic7ed), identity check passed (episode title matches; content confirms the gold-star accusation arc, blanket-hot-day gag, piano-in-the-tree, football teaching). Single row on dominant story per spec: the football-teaching montage that titles the episode and closes it, Linus teaching Sally, Peppermint Patty teaching Marcie, tryouts that end 'not good enough', and Lucy's tee with Charlie Brown falling for it 'again and again'. Coping left empty with reason: the pratfalls are played for laughs and no listed strategy is shown working. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: Peppermint Patty falsely accused of stealing the gold stars, vindicated when Snoopy's disguise finds the box in the wastebasket (injustice, honesty); Lucy pitching Schroeder's piano into the kite-eating tree and his replacement arriving. Topics anchored to the football story.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Chaos in the Classroom
rows.synopsis: There's "Chaos in the Classroom" when Sally brings Woodstock's nest to school for show and tell. And there's chaos on the field when Linus tries to teach Sally to play football.
rows.situation: Standing up for show and tell with a live helper who refuses to follow the plan.
rows.notes: Script tier: Gestdown subtitle transcript (Addic7ed), identity check passed (episode title matches; content confirms the bird's nest show and tell, letter practice, ruler arc, patrol arc, blanket truce, baseball close). Single row on dominant story per spec: Sally brings an authentic bird's nest to show and tell and invites its owner to explain the construction, and the classroom chaos follows. Coping anchors to asking for help (she recruits the nest's owner as her expert). Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: Linus borrowing and wrecking the ruler, then replacing it and owning the lesson about borrowing; Marcie made patrol person while Peppermint Patty's jealousy is named out loud ('I'm into jealousy, Chuck'), and both lose the post to exhaustion; Lucy's designer-jeans non-slide; Linus' closing gratitude speech and Charlie Brown's honest 'But I want to win!' (gratitude versus wanting to win, unnamed in the list). Topics anchored to the school story.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: It's That Team Spirit, Charlie Brown
rows.synopsis: Snoopy uses various techniques to get Linus' blanket. Peppermint Patty continues to struggle in school. Re-Run goes for a ride on his mother's bicycle. Charlie Brown tries to coach his baseball team.
rows.situation: Trying everything to hold a team together when nothing goes right and everyone walks away.
rows.notes: Script tier: Gestdown subtitle transcript (Addic7ed), identity check passed (episode title matches; content confirms signals and chatter, Lucy's fly-ball practice, the homemade telephone, the rain argument, Rerun's ride, Patty refusing school). Single row on dominant story per spec: Charlie Brown coaching the new season, inventing signals, chatter cards, and a telephone to right field, then standing alone in the rain as the team leaves. Coping anchors to trying again (his repeated attempts to build spirit and communication), and the episode's melancholy is recorded, not smoothed. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: Snoopy's schemes for Linus' blanket; Peppermint Patty refusing school until Marcie pulls the doghouse down and says outright that Snoopy is a beagle; Rerun's bicycle ride. Topics anchored to the baseball story.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Lucy Loves Schroeder
rows.synopsis: Charlie Brown tangles with the Kite-Eating Tree. Snoopy eats Sally's homework. The gang goes to summer camp. Lucy fawns over Schroder unsuccessfully. Something that goes bump in the night scares Snoopy, so he seeks help from Lucy.
rows.situation: Liking someone who never seems to notice you, and trying every way to be seen.
rows.notes: Script tier: Gestdown subtitle transcript (Addic7ed), identity check passed (episode title matches; content confirms the Lucy-Schroeder thread, kite-eating tree, camp, bumped-in-the-night watchdog arc). Single row on dominant story per spec: Lucy's long courtship of Schroeder, from saucepans to melodies to 'we're through', all against his silence. Coping anchors to talking it out (she says her feelings out loud, over and over); the note records honestly that nothing is resolved and he never notices. Age-band edge call: crush and marriage-talk satire reads older, tagged 8-10 on Batch 9's heavier-beat pattern. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: camp sends Charlie Brown home as a 'troublemaker' and he is delighted; Peppermint Patty cries in front of the little red-haired girl and Linus comforts her ('beauty is in the eye of the beholder'); Snoopy scared of things that go bump in the night asks Lucy's booth for help, gets a bill. Topics anchored to the piano-centered title story.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Snoopy and the Giant
rows.synopsis: Snoopy breaks his foot and must wear a cast. Meanwhile, Woodstock grows a beanstalk to the sky, where he and Snoopy meet a cookie-hoarding giant. Finally, the youngest of the Van Pelts has to deal with various problems.
rows.situation: Living with a broken foot in an itchy cast when all you want is your old routine back.
rows.notes: Script tier with identity flag: Forever Dreaming transcript (page titled by FD 'Snoopy's Brother Spike') content-matches catalog S2E1 (broken foot, cast, crutches, cat next door); FD's titles and numbering are offset and unreliable for this series, so the match is by content against the catalog synopsis. Dominant story: Snoopy's injury and cast. Coping anchors to patience (enduring 'quite a few weeks' as told to calm down). Topics left empty with reason: the cast story matches no controlled topic; the training-for-the-big-game line is incidental. The beanstalk and giant arcs named in the catalog synopsis are not present in the captured transcript text, so they were not tagged.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Snoopy's Brother Spike
rows.synopsis: Peppermint Patty asks Charlie Brown for help with her team. Linus waits up for the Great Pumpkin while Charlie Brown and Peppermint Patty go bowling. Snoopy's older brother Spike vists.
rows.situation: A brother from far away, thin and down on his luck, comes to stay and the household reshapes around him.
rows.notes: Script tier with identity flag: Forever Dreaming transcript (page titled by FD 'Snoopy's Robot') content-matches catalog S2E2 (popcorn-selling favor, pelican mascot, Halloween bowling with the Great Pumpkin, Spike's visit); FD titles and numbering are offset, match is by content. Dominant story: Spike's visit. Coping left empty with reason: the visit plays for comedy and care (Lucy fattens Spike up) without a listed strategy shown handling a feeling. Topics left empty with reason: the Spike story fits no controlled topic; the bowling and baseball threads carry Sports & games but are secondary arcs, not the story this row is about. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: Charlie Brown recruited to sell popcorn, then to wear the pelican costume, ending with Marcie's kiss as the head comes off; Linus keeping vigil in the pumpkin patch while everyone else bowls, and the real sighting arriving as a flying bowling ball.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Snoopy's Robot
rows.synopsis: The gang goes to computer camp. Linus starts a clinic for kids with security blankets. Snoopy goes to visit Spike in the desert. Charlie Brown and Peppermint Patty go on a date. Later Marcie and Peppermint Patty both develop a crush on Charlie Brown.
rows.situation: A first day somewhere full of unfamiliar machines, where every screen is a game nobody has played before.
rows.notes: Script tier with identity flag: Forever Dreaming transcript (page titled by FD 'Peppermint Patty's School Days') content-matches catalog S2E3 (computer camp, painting and checkers machines, game design, the robots-inside warning, Snoopy driving the bus); FD titles and numbering are offset, match is by content. Dominant story: the computer camp outing. Coping left empty with reason: the outing is a comic adventure with no coping beat shown. Topics left empty with reason: computer camp matches no controlled topic; School & books was weighed and rejected because camp is not school in this story. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: Linus' blanket-giving-up clinic (one enrollee, his sister's plant), the blanket lost in the desert and returned full of cactus stickers, Patty and Marcie's crush on Charlie Brown answered by a Navy enlistment letter, Peppermint Patty falling asleep and calling Chuck's name. Content consideration: Linus' attachment to the blanket is teased gently.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Peppermint Patty's School Days
rows.synopsis: Peppermint Patty's struggles in school are chronicled. Snoopy's develops a cool trick after his antics begin to wear on the kids' nerves. Schroeder doesn't know how to get to piano camp. The gang flies him there on Snoopy's doghouse.
rows.situation: Working hard at school and still landing at the bottom of the class.
rows.notes: Synopsis-fallback tier, synopsis-only: no verified transcript exists for this episode anywhere probed this session. Forever Dreaming's five Season 2 pages were all content-mapped, and none carries this episode's stories (its content sits offset across other pages); Gestdown was not re-probed for S2 after the S1 pass, so this row works from the catalog synopsis and title. Situation anchors Patty's chronic school struggle. Coping left empty with reason: the synopsis shows the struggle without a listed strategy handling it. Topics anchored to the school story. Content consideration: none beyond school frustration. Top-up pass 2026-11-14: re-fetched the Forever Dreaming page titled "02x04 - Peppermint Patty's School Days" (topic 204612) and content-mapped it to catalog S2E3's stories (computer camp, Linus's blanket clinic, Spike's desert, the crush arc), confirming FD's S2 offset; live Gestdown lookup for S2E4 returned an empty manifest. Still no script for this episode's stories. Attempt list extended; synopsis-fallback tier stands.

rows.series_title: The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show
rows.episode_title: Sally's Sweet Babboo
rows.synopsis: Charlie Brown reflects on his most memorable Christmas while Sally and Lucy prepare for Valentine's Day and Peppermint Patty writes an award-winning essay on Snoopy.
rows.situation: Sending a valentine to someone who keeps insisting he is not your valentine.
rows.notes: Script tier with identity flag: Forever Dreaming transcript (page titled by FD 'Sally's Sweet Babboo', the one FD title whose content matches its catalog title) content-matches catalog S2E5 (Christmas-play term paper retelling, the school valentine box with the sweet-babboo card, the essay contest win). Dominant story per title: Sally's valentine thread, ending on the shared line that valentines can be confusing and painful. Coping left empty with reason: the thread closes on commiseration (nobody got a valentine from the person they wanted) with no listed strategy shown handling the feeling. Age-band edge call: crush and valentine content reads older, tagged 8-10 consistent with S1E13. Topics left empty with reason: valentine and crush content fits none of the controlled eight. Secondary arcs noted, not tagged: the disastrous ice-rink Christmas play (Sally's one wrong word, Harold Angel at the door), Lucy's wreath sales pitched honestly and selling nothing, Charlie Brown's empty mailbox, Peppermint Patty's over-the-top Snoopy essay winning the all-city contest and collapsing off the stage.

Split-story row: tags anchored on the segment 1 story (the pageant), not the Wiz Kids story. Situation sits near starter term 'being different' with a specific twist (toughness versus cuteness). Coping anchors to trying again (the stumble in the dance-off answered by joust-dancing as themselves). Topics anchored to the dance-off finale.
